assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with atoms trapped at the magic wavelength so that light shifts cancel, turned atomic spectroscopy into a platform with fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This is a clear, original idea with decisive impact on metrology, tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and prospects for redefining the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye led the experimental demonstration and pushed accuracy and stability to the frontier. Other groups (Strontium/ytterbium efforts elsewhere) contributed, but two names give a clean and defensible configuration. I have scientific and community familiarity with this field and disclose that, though no personal collaboration with the credited names is claimed.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups worldwide, with agreement at the 1e-18 level and clock comparisons over fibre links. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, since the field is mature and still rapidly advancing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to credit the earlier ion-clock lineage already recognised in 2005 and 2012, or the lattice clock as a distinct invention.
Credit may be argued to extend to other lattice-clock pioneers not in the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Mott-insulator transition and now serve as controllable quantum simulators of Hubbard-type models, including single-site-resolved microscopy. The conceptual clarity, the control and the reach into many-body physics make this a high-impact field.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied key theory proposals, Greiner and Bloch the decisive early experiments and later quantum-gas microscopy. Esslinger is also credited elsewhere in the entry, and Jaksch (not supplied) was central to the original lattice proposal, so allocation is genuinely contestable; I choose the three above as the most defensible subset within the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced and extended the results over two decades, and the interpretation is firmly settled. Timing is appropriate, although some of the strongest simulation claims are still maturing.
uncertainties: Competing claims between the Mott-insulator, quantum-gas-microscope and fermionic-lattice lines.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered results beyond what classical computation can reach is still debated.
Omitted theory contributors such as Jaksch cannot be added from the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underpins superconducting quantum processors, dispersive readout and microwave quantum optics. The idea is original and its practical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal came from Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf; the first strong-coupling demonstration was by Wallraff and Schoelkopf and colleagues. Girvin is among the credited names and arguably deserves equal weight, so the three-name selection leaves a real allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and widely adopted. However, the 2025 prize recognised superconducting-circuit macroscopic quantum tunnelling, so timing and thematic overlap with a recent award need weighing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize and the question of how soon the same platform should be recognised again.
Allocation between theory (Girvin, Blais) and experiment (Wallraff, Schoelkopf) is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states, with large conceptual influence on condensed-matter and materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposal; Molenkamp led the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Zhang (deceased) and Bernevig/Hughes are outside the supplied credit, which complicates a complete historical account but still permits a fair three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many materials and experiments, and now a mature field. The recognition is timely, though some topological aspects (Thouless et al.) were already honoured in 2016.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize and the contribution of non-listed theorists.
Whether the quantum spin Hall experiment or the three-dimensional topological insulator is the prime discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision picture and the strong-field quantum theory of high-harmonic generation provided the physical basis for attosecond pulse generation. The model is simple, original and has lasting explanatory power across strong-field and attosecond physics.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's three-step model, the independent Schafer et al. work and the Lewenstein et al. quantum theory form a coherent set. I note professional proximity to this area (attosecond photoionisation theory and long collaboration with Anne L'Huillier) and disclose this; I do not claim a documented tie to these three. Credit would need to be weighed against the 2023 prize for attosecond pulses.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed, including in attosecond spectroscopy and tomography. However, the 2023 prize already recognised the experimental generation and measurement of attosecond pulses, so an additional prize on the theory must be justified as distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 prize may make a second award on the same theme hard to justify.
Allocation between the three-step model and the quantum theory is genuinely contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, and launched the field of twistronics and moire quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band at a magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues observed correlated insulating and superconducting states. The theory and experiment are cleanly separated, supporting a three-name configuration. Other experimental groups (e.g. Dean and co-workers on related moire systems) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the pairing mechanism and many correlated phases are not yet understood. The discovery is very recent and the physics is still evolving, so some caution about timing is warranted.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
The field is young, and whether the key claim will remain stable is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapped-ion quantum computing and simulation began with the Cirac-Zoller proposal and its experimental implementation, demonstrating high-fidelity gates, entanglement and digital quantum simulation. The impact on quantum information science is large.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the original proposal; Blatt led the principal demonstrations of gates and simulation with trapped ions. Wineland and Monroe are not listed, and the 2012 prize honoured Wineland for ion manipulation, so the allocation relative to prior recognition is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed in several laboratories. However, recognition overlaps with the 2012 prize and the field continues to move quickly toward scalable devices.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and the contributions of Wineland and Monroe.
Cirac and Zoller also appear in other entries on the list, so consistency of credit across entries should be considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP mapped the cosmic microwave background anisotropy with unprecedented precision and established the standard Lambda-CDM parameters, including the age and composition of the universe. The results are robust and had a major impact on cosmology.
assessment.attribution: The mission principal investigator was Bennett, with Page and Spergel central to instrument design and cosmological analysis. The collaboration was large and Wilkinson (deceased) was originally important, so a three-person selection is defensible but inherently selective.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed and superseded by Planck, so the results are very mature. The risk is that the cosmology prizes of 2006, 2011 and 2019 already recognised nearby themes, and WMAP's result is an instrument and survey achievement.
uncertainties: Whether a large-collaboration mission fits a three-person prize.
Overlap with earlier cosmology prizes and with Planck.
